correctness.rationale: Independently re-verified every headline inference. Q-smoothness Jacobian case split (x0=0 forces all xi=0; x0=1 gives x3=x4=0, x1,x2 in {0,-3/4}, dx0 q in {4,229/64,101/32} nonzero) is exact. S={x0=0,sum xi^4=0} smooth with gradient 4xi^3, hence quartic K3, transverse to H since dq and dx0 are independent on S. Total differential dF=q dx0+x0 dq+t dq5+q5 dt reduces to q5 dt on S at t=0, so C=S cap {q5=0} lies in Sing(X), proving non-semistability. Lagrange argument (a4xi^3+b5xi^4=0 forces all xi=0 given sum xi^4=0) proves C smooth; explicit point (0:1:zeta:u:eta u) with zeta=eta=exp(i pi/4), u^5=-(1+zeta^5)/(1+eta^5) satisfies both equations exactly in structure and to <4e-16 numerically with minor modulus ~15.3, re-ran PASS. Normal bundles O_S(4) tensor O_S(1)=O_S(5) nontrivial gives Friedman d-semistability failure. Headline does not claim general-fiber smoothness or the 1/202/1 table, honestly stating neither proved nor disproved, so the sketched uniform-epsilon patching is out of scope.
